clue.text: Wrongly interprets unusual smartness in dud

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets the wrong end of the stick about a failure who dresses unexpectedly well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual smartness in dud' reads as a description, but 'unusual' is the signal that the fourteen letters after it are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To misunderstand something is to take its meaning the wrong way, a straight synonym for wrongly interpreting.

clue.text: Male, I admit, who travels to work

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man confesses to being a commuter or a worker who moves abroad for jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant worker is a person who moves from place to place, often abroad, in search of employment.

clue.text: Darned slang, this? Wrong

indicators.note: the fifteen letters are put together the wrong way, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a suggestion that cursed slang counts as correct usage: surely not?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranging 'darned slang, this' gives the phrase, and the clue as a whole says that slang is the wrong idea of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard English is the accepted, formal variety of the language, the very opposite of swearing and slang.

clue.text: Move cautiously North-West? On the contrary

explanation.surface: A navigator is told to edge carefully to the north-west, then told the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' works twice over: it turns ON round, and it swaps North-West for its opposite point, South-East.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to advance slowly and carefully, as a car does when edging out of a junction.

explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of the main London railway terminals, so it is an example of a station.
